hook: Rome's first emperor, who found the city brick and left it marble.

pages.x: Gaius Octavius was a sickly 18-year-old when his great-uncle Julius Caesar was murdered in 44 BC. Caesar's will made him his adopted son and heir. Many laughed at "the boy", but he raised an army from Caesar's old soldiers and took the name Caesar.

He beat Caesar's killers together with Mark Antony, then turned on Antony. His friend and admiral Agrippa won the sea battle of Actium in 31 BC. Egypt, with its huge riches, became his own personal property.
pages.cap: Agrippa, the friend who won his battles

pages.x: In 27 BC he made a show of handing power back to the Senate, which gave him the title Augustus, "the revered one". He kept the outward forms of the Republic but held real power for 41 years, calling himself only "first citizen". The month of August is named after him.

He boasted that he had found Rome a city of brick and left it a city of marble. He gave Rome its first fire brigade and police, repaired its roads and aqueducts, and built new temples, a forum and the Altar of Peace.

His rule began the Pax Romana, two centuries of peace across most of the empire. He set up a professional army and a courier service, and counted the people of his empire. The Gospel of Luke says Jesus was born when a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be registered.

In AD 9 three Roman legions were wiped out in the Teutoburg Forest in Germany. The old emperor, a writer says, banged his head against a door, crying: "Quinctilius Varus, give me back my legions!" Rome never again tried to conquer Germany.

He died in AD 14, aged 75. At the end he asked his friends whether he had played his part well in the comedy of life, and, using the closing line of a play, asked them to applaud as he left the stage. The Senate declared him a god.

Augustus ended a century of civil wars and turned the Roman Republic into an empire that lasted five more centuries in the west and nearly fifteen in the east. He became the model of an emperor for ages after.
pts: Began two centuries of the Pax Romana
Gave his name to the month of August
